page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4-lssd is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes a 504 MB L3 cache, 31.0 GB of system memory providing 7.75 GB per core, and a bundled 137 GB local NVMe SSD. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2240.59 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1858.0. However, multi-core scaling is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 4549.86 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 4215.0. Memory performance exhibits a notable bottleneck, with large-block read bandwidth dropping to 22.46 GB/sec, though small-block cached reads reach 334.26 GB/sec. The server demonstrates strong single-threaded text processing and gzip compression performance. For database workloads, Redis SET operations achieve an average throughput of 7.38 million operations per second, while Passmark database operations score in the lower quartile.

This instance type provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The integrated 137 GB local NVMe SSD offers low-latency scratch space, though the overall storage capacity is modest. Due to the weak multi-core scaling and poor large-block memory bandwidth, this server is best suited for lightweight database hosting, caching layers, single-threaded text processing, and moderate memory-intensive applications rather than heavy parallel computing or large-scale LLM text generation.
